chunks: My father (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to me from Sa'd ibn Abdillah, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, and Ya'qub ibn Yazid, and Musa ibn 'Umar, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Abu al-Hasan al-Rida (peace be upon him), who said:
I asked, 'How should I say peace upon the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) at his grave?' He said, 'You say:'

Peace upon the Messenger of Allah. Peace to you and the mercy of Allah and His blessings. Peace to you, O Messenger of Allah! Peace to you, O Muhammad ibn Abdillah! Peace to you, O chosen one of Allah! Peace to you, O beloved of Allah! Peace to you, O choice of Allah! Peace to you, O trustee of Allah!

I testify that you are the Messenger of Allah and I testify that you are Muhammad ibn Abdillah, and I testify that you have advised your nation, and you strove in the way of Allah [your Lord], and you worshipped Him until certainty (death) came to you.
So may Allah reward you with the best reward that He has given any prophet for his nation.

O Allah, send blessings upon Muhammad and his family [and the family of Muhammad] with the best blessings You sent upon Ibrahim and the family of Ibrahim. Verily You are the Praiseworthy, the Glorified.
ai.seo_question: What is the correct way to say Salam to the Prophet at his grave according to Imam al-Rida?
ai.summary: Recorded in Ibn Qulawayh’s *Kamil al-Ziyarat*, this hadith from Imam al-Rida (AS) outlines a comprehensive liturgical formula for visiting the Prophet’s grave, emphasizing both personal salutation and theological affirmation. It uniquely combines direct address with the Shahada and a supplication for superior blessings (*afdala*), reflecting the Shia emphasis on the Prophet’s enduring spiritual presence and his familial connection to Ibrahim. This practice underscores the concept of *Ziyarat* as an act of worship that reinforces the believer's bond with the Prophet and, by extension, the Ahl al-Bayt.

en.sayyid-mohsen-al-husayni-al-milani: 10. My father narrated to me from Sa’d ibn ‘Abdillāh, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn ‘Isā, Ya’qūb ibn Yazīd, and Mūsā ibn ‘Umar, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn Abī Nasr, who said:
I asked Abal Ḥasan (Imam Riďā (a.s.)), “How should I say Salām to the Messenger of Allah (s.a.a.w.) next to his grave?” Imam (a.s.) replied: Recite (the following):

Salām upon the Messenger of Allāh. Salām to you and (may) Allāh’s Mercy and Blessings be upon you.                                Salām to you, O Messenger of Allāh! Salām to you, O Muḥammad ibn ‘Abdillāh! Salām to you, O chosen one from the creation of Allāh! Salām to you, O love of Allāh! Salām to you, O choice of Allāh! Salām to you, O trustee of Allāh!

I testify that you are the Messenger of Allāh and that you are Muḥammad, son of ‘Abdillāh. I testify that you advised your nation, you fought in the way of your Lord, and you worshipped Him until that which is certain (death) came to you.
May Allāh reward you with a greater reward than He has given to any (other) prophet for guiding his nation.

O Allāh! Send Your blessing on Muḥammad and the family of Muḥammad, (blessings which are) greater than that which You sent on Ibrāhīm and the family of Ibrāhīm. Verily You are the Praised, the Glorified.
